title: Uniform tower pullback domains and the completed reconstruction counit
statement:
Fix the global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ for $n\geq1$. All schemes are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Write $\mathcal C_T=\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ for the ordinary derived category of strict varying-coefficient towers restricted to constructible levels with common finite cohomological and Tor intervals [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Write $r^D_{n,m}:D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\to D_m$ for its derived reduction map, $m\leq n$ [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]; normalized means all these maps are invertible.

For every $h:U\to V$ between these schemes, let $h_\bullet^*$ be exact finite constant-ring pullback levelwise [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Then $U,V$ are Noetherian, every $D\in\mathcal C_V$ is bounded below in the ordinary tower derived category, and every finite evaluation $D_n$ admits bounded constructible etale origin [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]. The functor $h_\bullet^*$ preserves $\mathcal C_V$, each common cohomological interval and each common Tor interval. There are canonical isomorphisms
$$h_m^*(D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)\simeq(h_n^*D_n)\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m,$$
natural in $D$ and in successive quotients, under which
$$r^{h_\bullet^*D}_{n,m}=h_m^*(r^D_{n,m}).$$
In particular $h_\bullet^*$ preserves normalized towers.

For $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ let $R_T=\varprojlim_n(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_T$ be the completed coefficient sheaf and $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,\mathbf Z_\ell)$ the derived-complete constructible category [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Write $r_T=\operatorname{red}_T$, $L_T=R\varprojlim$, with unit $\iota_T$ and counit $\kappa_T:r_TL_T\to\mathrm{id}$, for [det-sp-normalized-equivalence]. Completed pullback $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ means [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For every $K\in\mathcal I_V$, $C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK$ is normalized constructible, $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K=L_UC_K$ under the definition's single-resolution quotient-tower identification, and $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K\in\mathcal I_U$. The canonical natural comparison of actual derived towers is
$$\alpha_{h,K}:r_Uh^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K=r_UL_UC_K\xrightarrow{\kappa_{U,C_K}}C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK,$$
and it is invertible.

source.place: Proof (1), domains and etale-origin input; (2), pullback of reductions; (3), whole-tower pullback reduction comparisons

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, so ascending chains stabilize. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian and the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma applies to $U$ and $V$. Choose common cohomological bounds $[a,b]$ for $D$. Exact evaluation commutes with cohomology, so $(\mathcal H^iD)_n=\mathcal H^i(D_n)=0$ for $i<a$. A tower sheaf whose every level is zero is zero, since its objects and maps are levelwise. Thus $D\in D^{\ge a}(\operatorname{Tow}(V,\mathcal O_E))$. Each $D_n$ is bounded intrinsically constructible. Apply clause (ii) of the constructible-origin equivalence to obtain a bounded constructible etale $L_n$ and an isomorphism $\nu_V^*L_n\simeq D_n$. Its coefficient convention uses uniformizer powers: if $e$ is the ramification index, $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{en})$, so its index is $en\ge1$. This supplies precisely the required etale-origin witness.

source.place: Tag 09AL (lemma-compare-constructible-derived); morphisms.tex Tag 01T6; levelwise cohomology argument

proof.text: Use the canonical constant-section identifications at every $A_n$. They commute with quotient maps: both composites send the constant section $a$ to its residue class, and sheafification determines the resulting maps uniquely. Exact finite-ring pullback therefore sends a strict semilinear tower to a strict semilinear tower. Kernels and cokernels are levelwise, so it is an exact tower functor and its termwise derived functor is $h_\bullet^*$. Its evaluation is $h_n^*D_n$. The uniform-tower clause of [lem-sp-proetale-ctf-pullback-domains] applies with $v=h$ and $K_\bullet=D$, without normalization: the schemes, finite rings and ordinary constant-ring derived categories are exactly its hypotheses. It gives constructible levels and preserves each chosen common cohomological interval and Tor interval, hence $h_\bullet^*D\in\mathcal C_U$.

source.place: Proof (1)-(2), finite pullback domains and levelwise construction

proof.text: For $A_n\to A_m$ apply the unbounded coefficient-pullback model to $K=D_n$. Invert its canonical isomorphism to obtain $h_m^*(D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m)\simeq h_n^*D_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$ in the $A_m$ derived category. This is natural in $D_n$, hence in $D$. The stated model is the identity on local pure tensors after the constant-ring identifications. For $j\le m\le n$, both successive-quotient comparisons, under tensor associativity, send a generator $(x\otimes a)\otimes b$ to $x\otimes\bar a b$. Thus they agree, including $m=n$, where the map is the unit identification. This proves compatibility in the quotients without requiring a quotient map to be flat.

source.place: Tag 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), coefficient-pullback application; balanced tensor calculation

proof.text: Represent $D$ by a complex of strict towers $C_\bullet$ and write $t:C_n\to\operatorname{Res}C_m$ for its composite transition. Take a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to C_n$. The reduction $r^D_{n,m}$ is the derived adjunct of $t$; the normalized scalar adjunction computes it by $P\otimes_{A_n}A_m\to C_m$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,t(x)$, where $t$ includes $P\to C_n$. Exact $h_n^*$ carries this resolution to a flat-term K-flat representative of $h_n^*D_n$. For the pulled-back transition, the same adjunct formula is $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,h^*t(x)$. The coefficient comparison of step 3 identifies this with $h_m^*$ of the first formula. Therefore $r^{h_\bullet^*D}_{n,m}=h_m^*(r^D_{n,m})$ under the asserted isomorphism. This is an equality of derived arrows computed on representatives, not an inference from equality of their cohomology maps. If $D$ is normalized, every right-hand map is invertible; hence so is every reduction of $h_\bullet^*D$, which proves normalization preservation.

Now take $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $K\in\mathcal I_V$. The constructible restriction of the reduction/limit equivalence applies because $V$ is Noetherian by step 1 and $\ell$ is invertible on a $k$-scheme. It gives $r_VK\in\mathcal C_V$ normalized. Steps 2 and 4 then give $C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK\in\mathcal C_U$ normalized. Applying the constructible restriction of $L_U$ gives $L_UC_K\in\mathcal I_U$, since $U$ is also Noetherian.

source.place: Statement, normalized constructible restriction of red and R lim

proof.text: Choose one flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ as in the definition of integral pullback. By the strict coefficient-tensor descent (with $R=R_V$, $S_n=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_V$), which supplies the reduction functor of the reduction-tower statement, $r_VK$ is represented in the ordinary tower derived category by the strict complex tower $P_n=P\otimes_{R_V}(\mathbf Z/\ell^n)_V$, with the actual quotient-induced transitions $x\otimes c\mapsto x\otimes\bar c$, naturally in $K$ and independently of $P$. Exact levelwise pullback, applied termwise, therefore represents $C_K$ by the strict complex tower $Q=(h_n^*P_n)_n$, with those same pulled-back transitions. By definition the completed pullback is the product-cone model $\mathsf C(\operatorname{Res}Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ of precisely this tower after restricting scalars to $R_U$. Countable products of $R_U$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ are exact, so the strict Roos comparison gives the natural isomorphism $\rho:\mathsf C(\operatorname{Res}Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim\operatorname{Res}Q$, normalized through a K-injective tower resolution and compatible with the projections to the levels. The right side is $L_UC_K$ under the adjunction's definition of $L_U$ (forget scalars to $R_U$, then total derived limit). Thus the single-resolution identification $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K=L_UC_K$ is $\rho$, at the level of actual derived objects and with their whole tower; no claim that separately chosen finite-level representatives determine a derived tower is used. Resolution independence and functoriality of the integral construction are those of the well-definedness statement for integral operations, and $\rho$ and the descent comparisons are natural for derived morphisms, so the identification is natural in $K$.

source.place: Definitions 3.5.2-3.5.3, Lemma 3.5.7; single-resolution formula in def-pur-integral-derived-operations

proof.text: Under step 6 apply the counit of $r_U\dashv L_U$ to $C_K$: its source is $r_UL_UC_K=r_Uh^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K$ and its target is $C_K=h_\bullet^*r_VK$. This defines the displayed $\alpha_{h,K}$ as a morphism in the ordinary derived category of strict coefficient towers. The counit is an isomorphism on normalized towers, and $C_K$ is normalized by step 5, so $\alpha_{h,K}$ is invertible. Counit naturality, composed with the functors $h_\bullet^*r_V$ and the single-resolution identification, gives the asserted natural comparison in $K$. Step 5 and step 6 also give $h^*_{\mathbf Z_\ell}K\in\mathcal I_U$.

source.place: Statement, counit on normalized towers; Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 3.5.7

tool_uses.why: Generic finite-type Noetherian permanence proves the hypotheses of the reconstruction equivalence; no geometric route is replaced.
Generic exact-evaluation/cohomology compatibility justifies boundedness in the ordinary derived tower category.
The finite coefficient bounded constructible site equivalence supplies the etale-origin witness at each level; no same-unit node states that equivalence.
Generic inverse-image/change-of-ring comparison, with its pure-tensor normalization, supplies the coefficient square for arbitrary finite quotient rings.
Generic existence of a flat-term K-flat resolution computes a derived coefficient adjunct at one level.
Generic derived scalar adjunction with its prescribed generator formula identifies the actual pulled-back reduction arrow.
Generic resolution independence for the exact single-resolution definition of completed pullback; used only to identify that construction with the limit of the whole quotient tower.
